title: Two by two (Mark 6:7–29)
hookLine: the twelve go out with a staff and no bread; John the Baptist is killed at a party

lines: AND A STORY IN THE MIDDLE.
cards: The extra charger. The spare sweater. A backup plan for the backup plan.
Most of us pack for everything that could go wrong. Now imagine being told to pack nothing. No bag.
No food. No money. One walking stick and the sandals on your feet.
That's how Jesus sends out the twelve apostles for the first time. And while they're out on the road, Mark tells what happened to the man who went before them all.

teach.b: First, two by two. Jesus calls the twelve and sends them out in pairs. Mark doesn't say why.
Jewish law said a matter was confirmed by two witnesses, and there's a simpler reason too: nobody should walk alone. Second, the packing list.

teach.h: A STAFF ONLY, NO BREAD, NO MONEY.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And he commanded them that they should take nothing for the way, but a staff only; no scrip, no bread, nor money in their purse". A scrip is a traveler's bag. Sandals, yes; two coats, no.
Stay in whatever house takes you in. If a town won't hear you, shake the dust off your feet and move on.

They go, preach that people should repent, and anoint many sick people with oil and heal them. Catholics see in that anointing a first glimpse of the sacrament of the anointing of the sick. Third, the story in the middle.
While the twelve are out, Mark cuts away, another sandwich, to King Herod. John the Baptist had told Herod he had no right to marry his brother's wife, Herodias, and Herod had him locked up.
Herod feared John, and liked to listen to him, though it troubled him.
At Herod's birthday party, the daughter of Herodias dances, and the king, showing off for his guests, swears to give her anything. Her mother tells her what to ask for: John's head on a dish.
Herod is sorry, but won't break his oath in front of his guests. John is beheaded in prison, and his disciples come and bury him. Fourth, why here?
Mark puts the cost of the mission right in the middle of the mission.

teach.h: TAKE NOTHING FOR THE WAY, BUT A STAFF ONLY.
teach.b: The ones sent out with nothing need to know how the messenger before them ended.

how: Catholics keep the Passion of Saint John the Baptist on August 29, and the Church's missionaries and religious orders have long taken the sending of the twelve as a model of simple living; the sick receive the sacrament of anointing with blessed oil.

o: a small coin carried for the road toll
a traveler's bag, left behind on the mission
a written permit to preach in a town

games.q: you're one of the twelve, about to be sent out on the road. what does Jesus tell you to take?
o: a bag, some bread and a little money.
games.why: "take nothing for the way, but a staff only; no scrip, no bread, nor money in their purse" and sandals, and one coat.

practice: Picture everything you're carrying into today, not in your bag but in your head: the backup plans, the worst-case scenarios, the grudge from yesterday. Pick one thing and imagine setting it down by the door.
If you pray, trust God with it, the way the twelve had to trust strangers for their bread; if you don't, just practice walking out without it.

wordCard.voice: Scrip. A traveler's bag, one of the things Jesus told the twelve to leave behind. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: two, two, Mark's way of saying in pairs.

carryVoice: Your line: take nothing for the way. A staff, sandals, and someone walking beside you. See you tomorrow.
